focus: The 36 HVR hard blockers in sk-code SKILL.md and the 500 ms hook stdin deadline without a late-write test
noveltyJustification: Four new findings: the exact punctuation inventory behind the 36 blockers, the two deadline constants and six short-budget consumers with their documented-but-unmeasured basis, the missing late-write test proved from the helper's write timing plus the recorded limitation, and the two compounding gaps.
keyQuestions: Q7: Why does .skilled/skills/sk-code/SKILL.md carry 36 HVR hard blockers, and what does the 500 ms hook stdin deadline against a 3 s hook budget risk?
answeredQuestions: Q7: Why does .skilled/skills/sk-code/SKILL.md carry 36 HVR hard blockers, and what does the 500 ms hook stdin deadline against a 3 s hook budget risk?
ruledOut: Lowering every deadline to the host budget - trades a silent loss for a killed hook with the same unmeasured uncertainty
A configurable per-host deadline - no host exposes its write latency or budget, so the option would have no input

label: The 36 HVR hard blockers are 27 semicolons and 9 em dashes in the always-loaded hub SKILL.md; the shipped scanner prints the breakdown (x27 hard punctuation ';', x9 hard punctuation em dash), the epic recorded the same count at multiple checkpoints and left it while sweeping other files to zero. Smallest fix: one punctuation sweep proved by the scanner printing hard blockers: 0.

SHORT_HOST_STDIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 500 is defined twice (shared-stdin.ts:23, hook-adapter-shared.mjs:17) and serves the Claude user-prompt-submit shim, session-prime, compact-inject, both spec-gate-classify adapters and the Codex session-start/user-prompt-submit adapters; the 3 s host budget is documented in the hooks README and the v2.7.2.0 changelog, and the value is an unmeasured judgment (no host write latency was ever measured). Smallest fix: choose the semantics (keep-drop versus first-byte deadline) before editing one constant.

There is no late-write test: runHook writes the payload immediately after spawn when holdOpen is set, and the short-deadline payload test at hook-stdin-deadline.test.mjs:225 therefore proves only an immediate write; the round-four Known Limitation 2 states that a payload written more than 500 ms after the hook starts on a held-open stdin is cut short and the hook takes its empty answer. Smallest fix: add one case writing at ~800 ms and pin the outcome, so the drop is visible before any deadline change.

Two recorded gaps compound the deadline risk: a held-open stdin plus a child that runs to its own 2500-2800 ms timeout still exceeds the host's 3 s (Known Limitation 1), and the compiled shim's 1 MB overflow path is covered by no suite (Known Limitation 3, manual 2.2 MB probe only).
